passage: The client deck was due at five, and the printer had jammed, when Shreya leaned over Manjula's cubicle. "Have you heard? Ritesh's team is telling the director we're slow. We should tell her about their missed audit first." Manjula's phone buzzed. Two people in the pantry were already picking sides. She felt the pull to pass on a tale, just to be safe. "I'll pass on that," she said. "I'll say hi to Ritesh's team tomorrow like always. Can you check page six with me? The chart is wrong." Shreya shrugged, a little disappointed, but bent over the page. The deck went out at 4:58.

qa.q: What time did the deck go out?
What was Manjula tempted to do, and why?
qa.a: Manjula felt the pull to pass on a tale about the other team, just to be safe.

qa.q: How did Manjula stay friendly to everyone without taking sides?
qa.a: She declined to pass on the gossip, planned to greet Ritesh's team as usual, and turned Shreya's attention back to fixing the chart.

qa.q: How might Shreya see Manjula's refusal?
qa.a: Shreya seemed a little disappointed, perhaps expecting an ally, yet still helped with page six.

grounding: Gossip and groups pull a colleague in; she stays friendly to all, does good work and avoids taking sides.

passage:
With the team lead on leave and the quarter-end report due on Friday, the analytics floor in Kochi had split into two camps: Francis's "old team" and the new hires who sat by the window. Every lunch, someone pulled Wasim aside.
"You're with us, right?" Francis said on Tuesday, walking him to the canteen. "Those window guys say you copy their queries. Tell me what they say about me, so I know."
Wasim felt the pull. Francis's side would be safer; he had been here five years.
"I'll be honest, Francis. I'm not going to carry what anyone says," Wasim said. "Not to you, not to them."
Francis's face cooled. "Suit yourself."
That week Wasim ate lunch with the window group on Wednesday and at Francis's table on Thursday, and spent his evenings fixing the broken data pipeline everyone had avoided. When the report went out on time on Friday, the lead, back from leave, asked who had fixed the pipeline. Both camps said, "Wasim."

qa.q: When was the quarter-end report due?
What did Wasim feel when Francis asked him to report back?
qa.a: Tempted to side with Francis, since that felt safer with Francis's five years in the team.

qa.q: How did Wasim stay out of the office politics?
qa.a: He refused to carry tales, ate lunch with both groups, and put his effort into fixing the broken pipeline.

qa.q: How did Francis react to Wasim's refusal?
qa.a: Coolly ("Suit yourself"), disappointed not to gain an ally.

grounding: Shows office groups pulling a newcomer in, and staying friendly to all, doing good work and refusing to pass tales.

passage:
In his third month at the insurance office in Gurugram, Naveen saw how things worked: Deepika's lunch group mocked the new regional manager, and the manager rewarded whoever brought him news.
On Monday Deepika said, laughing, "Rastogi sir thinks spreadsheets are a personality." Naveen laughed too. That afternoon, alone with Rastogi sir at the printer, he felt the urge to mention it, casually. It would make him look loyal. It might even get him the client visit he wanted.
He opened his mouth, then closed it. He thought about sitting next to Deepika afterwards.
Instead he said, "Sir, I've finished the claims review early. Can I take the Faridabad client visit?"
Rastogi sir looked at the report, nodded, and said yes.
At lunch the next day Deepika started another joke. Naveen smiled, said, "Let's give him a month," and changed the subject to cricket. Nobody at the table seemed to mind.

qa.q: What did Deepika say about Rastogi sir?
qa.a: "Rastogi sir thinks spreadsheets are a personality."

qa.q: Why was Naveen tempted to repeat Deepika's joke to Rastogi sir?
qa.a: He wanted to look loyal and hoped it might win him the client visit, a pull towards safety through tale-carrying.

qa.q: How did Naveen stay friendly to all without taking sides?
qa.a: He kept the joke to himself, earned the visit by finishing the review early, and gently steered the lunch table away from gossip.

qa.q: How might Deepika feel if she learned Naveen had passed on the joke?
qa.a: Betrayed and exposed, unable to trust him at the lunch table again.

grounding: Illustrates office gossip and the temptation to pass tales for safety, and choosing good work and friendliness to all instead.
